sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
The tests pass with this command, run from the project root (`<run>\work\L1\c\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both tests pass (`test_transfer_preserves_total` and `test_rejects_non_positive_amount`).

Without `PYTHONPATH=src` the run fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledgerlite'`. The package sits under `src/` and isn't installed, so Python can't find it. I didn't change any files.

In PowerShell or cmd, `PYTHONPATH=src python ...` won't work. Set the variable first with `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"` in PowerShell, or `set PYTHONPATH=src` in cmd. The command above is for the Git Bash shell I ran it in.

actions.command: cd <run>/work/L1/c/w && PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v 2>&1 | tail -15

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero. Otherwise it removes the account. Closing a name that doesn't exist raises `KeyError`, as `balance()` already does.

I added `test_close_requires_zero_balance` to `tests/test_ledger.py`. It checks that closing a non-zero account raises `ValueError` and leaves the account in place. It then checks that the account closes once its balance is back to zero.

The full suite passes: 3 tests, all OK. I ran it with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests`.
